meta_title: alig.tech: managed databases, high availability and security hardening
meta_description: Monitoring, root cause analysis, high availability setup and CIS-based hardening for PostgreSQL and SQL Server. MySQL is on the roadmap. The agent recommends, you approve.
hero_h1: When your database goes down, we tell you why, with the evidence.
hero_lead: alig.tech watches your PostgreSQL and SQL Server estate with an AI agent, finds the root cause and recommends the fix. Changes happen with your approval, or as routine jobs you approved in advance.
con_note: Sample output, made-up data. The format resembles patronictl list.
con_hint: Stop the leader and watch what the agent finds.
tl_0: db-demo-01 is not answering the Patroni API or PostgreSQL.
tl_1: The leader key in Consul expired.
tl_2: db-demo-02 has the most advanced WAL position and won the election.
tl_3: db-demo-02 was promoted. The timeline moved from 7 to 8.
tl_4: The HAProxy health check moved traffic to db-demo-02.
tl_5: db-demo-03 started following the new leader.
find_finding: The failover completed as expected. The old leader, db-demo-01, is down and the cluster has one replica left.
find_evidence: The timeline moved from 7 to 8 and db-demo-03 is streaming with 0 MB of lag. Some WAL that db-demo-01 wrote before it stopped may not have reached the replicas.
find_risk: If db-demo-01 is started as it is, the cluster ends up with two diverging histories. With a single replica, a second failure can stop the service.
find_advice: Resync db-demo-01 to the new leader with pg_rewind and rejoin it as a replica. Rollback: stop db-demo-01 and rebuild the replica with pgBackRest.
approval_wait: Waiting for approval. This change is not made until you approve it.
decision_approved: Approved. Because this is a demo, no command was run.
audit_note: Each row's digest also covers the digest before it. If one row changes, the chain breaks. Digests are computed in your browser.
audit_broken: Chain is broken: the digest of row {n} does not match.

svc5_text: Version upgrades, migrations and performance tuning.

page_saglik-taramasi_desc: A read-only, evidence-based health check for your PostgreSQL estate. Run the script on your own network, inspect the output, get the report.
tarama_lead: A read-only script running on your own network collects settings and statistics from your PostgreSQL estate. You read the file and upload it, and we return a report with evidence. We never connect to your database from outside.
tarama_s1: Download the collector script (alig-toplayici.py, Python 3.9 or later, no extra packages).
tarama_s2: Run it on a machine that can reach the database. An unprivileged role that is a member of pg_monitor is enough. The script sends nothing over the network and writes one JSON file.
tarama_s3: Open and read the JSON file. With --maskele, database, table and role names are replaced with aliases.
tarama_s4: Upload the file below. The report link is given immediately.
tarama_never_h: What it does and does not do
tarama_n1: Only fixed, reviewed SELECT queries run. The session is opened read-only with a 15-second limit per query.
tarama_n2: The contents of your tables are not read. Only catalogue, statistics and settings views are.
tarama_n3: The password is never passed to the script or written to the file. The file holds no connection details.
tarama_n4: Rules produce the report and every finding shows its evidence. No AI model produces findings.
tarama_n5: Reports are deleted after 30 days. You can delete yours at once from the report page.
tarama_f_ok: I am authorised to have this database scanned.
tarama_direct: A direct-connection mode (you give connection details, we scan) is not available yet. SQL Server and MySQL are on the roadmap.
tarama_f_mail_note: We store your company name and email address to link the scan to your record and to apply the limit of 2 free scans per company in 30 days.
hz_lead: What your team needs to prepare before starting a health check: a read-only account opened only for this job, a machine to run the script on, and six steps. You can share this guide with your database administrator and your information security team.
hz_need_1d: A database administrator who can create roles. They open the scan account once and remove it when the scan is done.
hz_need_2d: A separate role named alig_hc that is a member of pg_monitor only. Do not use a personal account, an application account or a superuser.
hz_need_3d: A machine with Python 3.9 or later and the psql client installed that can reach the database port. No extra packages are installed.
hz_need_4d: The script does not go out to the internet, so this machine needs no internet access. You upload the file from any machine that has a browser.
hz_need_5d: The queries are written for PostgreSQL 13–18. The script and report were tested on a real PostgreSQL 16 server. Run the scan on the primary (read-write) server.
hz_need_6d: Your company name and corporate email address. Each company gets 2 free scans per 30 days.
hz_s1_p: Download the ready-made SQL file and run it with an account that can create roles. The file changes no data. It only creates the alig_hc role and asks you for a password at the end.
hz_s1_what: The file does only what these lines say:
hz_s1_note: The password is not in the file. psql asks for it without showing it on screen. The account expires on its own after seven days and can open at most two connections at a time.
hz_s2_p: Allow the account to connect only from the machine where you will run the script. Add a line like the one below to pg_hba.conf with your own address, then reload the configuration:
hz_s2_pg: Do not give the password on the command line. Write it in this form to the .pgpass file in the home directory of the user who runs the script, and set the file mode to 600:
hz_s2_note: The script does not accept a password on the command line. The PGPASSWORD environment variable also works, but the .pgpass file is preferred.
hz_s3_p: After downloading the script, compute its SHA-256 digest and compare it with the value below. If the digests differ, do not run the script.
hz_s4_p: The script runs the fixed query list in a read-only session and writes alig-toplama.json to the current directory. It sends nothing over the network.
hz_s4_note: The --maskele option replaces database, schema, table, index, role and slot names with aliases. Remove it if you want the names to appear in the report.
hz_s4_db: Pass your application's database to --dbname. Table, index and sequence checks only run in the connected database; server-wide checks (version, connections, replication slots, archiving, TLS, roles) always cover the whole server. If you have several application databases, run the script once for each.
hz_s5_p: alig-toplama.json is plain text, so you can open and read it before uploading. When you are satisfied, upload it on the health check page with your company name and corporate email address. You get the report link right away.
hz_s5_cta: Go to the health check page
hz_s6_p: When the scan is done, remove the account and delete the line you added to pg_hba.conf. For a new scan you can open the account again with the same file.
hz_scope_h: What the scan account can and cannot see
hz_scope_y2: Table and index statistics (row counts, size, usage)
hz_scope_y3: Session, replication slot and archiving status
hz_scope_n3: Create roles, tables or other objects
hz_scope_n4: Password hashes and files on the server
hz_scope_note: The one check that reads password hashes (passwords stored with MD5) needs a superuser. With this account that check appears in the report as "not measured: privilege". It is not shown as clean. This table describes the account's own privileges. Privileges you granted to PUBLIC, and the default CREATE privilege on the public schema in PostgreSQL 14 and earlier, apply to every role. The scan checks that public schema privilege separately.
hz_sec_h: Summary for your information security team
hz_sec_1: alig.tech does not connect to your database. The only thing that connects is the script you run on your own network.
hz_sec_2: Every query that runs is fixed and published. The SHA-256 digests of the script and the query list are shown on the page.
hz_sec_3: The session is opened read-only. There is a 15-second limit per query and a 2-second limit for lock waits.
hz_sec_4: The file holds no connection details, passwords or table contents. You can review it before uploading.
hz_sec_5: The report is deleted after 30 days, and you can delete it right away from the report page. Findings are produced by rules, not by an AI model.
hz_a1: That check needs a superuser. It is expected with the scan account and does not affect the other findings.
hz_q2: The script says psql was not found.
hz_a2: Install the PostgreSQL client package, or give the full path to psql with the --psql option.
hz_q3: Can I run it on a standby server?
hz_a3: Some checks do not run on a standby and appear in the report as not measured. Run it on the primary for a complete result.
hz_a4: The file may be over the 5 MB limit, edited by hand, or produced by an old version of the script. Download the script again and rerun it. If you have used your 2 scans in 30 days, contact us.
hz_a5: The report states which database the table and index checks ran in and how many databases the server has. For the others, run the script again with --dbname and upload each file separately.
